pages.text: $(li)Press Cherenkov quartz into a $(item)Lattice Seed$().$(li)Grow a $(item)Boule$() in the $(item)Lattice Growth Vat$().$(li)Slice it into 16 $(item)Wafers$() with the $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$().$(li)Engrave in the $(item)Quantum Lithographer$() with $(fluid)Photoresist$().$(li)Cut each engraved wafer into 8 $(item)Dies$().

The lithographer needs a $(thing)lens$() in one input slot. Lenses are $(thing)catalysts$(): never consumed. Better lenses engrave better logic:$(br)$(li)Photonic Lens$(li)Metamaterial Sheet$(li)Dark Matter Lens$(li)Tesseract Lens$(li)Cosmic String Lens

Day 21. Why Cherenkov quartz? Cherenkov light is the blue glow a charged particle gives off when it outruns light in a medium - never in vacuum, but in water or glass, where light is slower. Every chip in this journal starts from that crystal.
A single crystal of Cherenkov quartz, grown in superfluid helium. Ready to be sliced.$(br2)Made in $(item)Lattice Growth Vat$().
A wafer sliced from a Cherenkov boule.$(br2)Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$().
Engraved with waveguides instead of wires.$(br2)Made in $(item)Quantum Lithographer$().
A single photonic logic die.$(br2)Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$().
